standard_prerequisites.name: The same-chapter decomposition of the associated points of a quasi-coherent module on a scheme over a locally Noetherian base into the associated points of the fibres and the generic points of the fibres
standard_prerequisites.use: It is the tool that lets the associated points upstairs be written as a union indexed by the associated points of the fibre downstairs.

standard_prerequisites.name: Fibres of a locally finite type morphism over the residue field of a point are locally Noetherian, cited from the morphisms chapter
standard_prerequisites.use: Makes the cited decomposition applicable to the fibre at the chosen point.

standard_prerequisites.name: The residue field tensor product of a field extension is Noetherian and Cohen-Macaulay, and in such a ring the associated primes are exactly the minimal primes, cited from the algebra chapter
standard_prerequisites.use: Shows that the associated points of the fibre of the base changed morphism over the chosen point are precisely its generic points, which is the remaining step of the argument.

standard_prerequisites.name: Flatness of the morphism between the two fibres, which is a base change of residue field extensions
standard_prerequisites.use: Identifies the pullback of the module on the fibre with the module on the base changed fibre.

core_obligations: Reduce to fibres: consider the morphism between the fibres at the chosen points, which is flat because it is a base change along a field extension, and observe that the module upstairs is the pullback of the module on the fibre downstairs (proof lines 1140-1146).

Apply the decomposition of associated points: since the fibre downstairs is locally Noetherian, the cited decomposition writes the associated points of the base changed fibre as the union, over the associated points of the fibre downstairs, of the associated points of the fibre of the morphism of fibres at that point (proof lines 1146-1149).

Identify the remaining pieces: the fibre of the morphism of fibres at the point is the spectrum of the tensor product of the two residue fields, whose associated primes are its minimal primes because that ring is Noetherian and Cohen-Macaulay, so its associated points are exactly its generic points, which is the condition in the statement (proof lines 1151-1167).
proof_roadmap: Base change to the residue fields and use the fibre point of view, where the module upstairs is a flat pullback from the fibre downstairs (proof lines 1140-1146).

Decompose the associated points of the fibre upstairs through the cited decomposition, and identify the associated points of each residue field tensor product as its generic points by Cohen-Macaulayness (proof lines 1146-1167).
difficulty_reason: The lemma computes the relative associated points after an arbitrary base change for a morphism locally of finite type: a point upstairs is associated relative to the new base exactly when its image downstairs is associated relative to the old base and the point is a generic point of an irreducible component of the tensor product of the two residue fields (statement lines 1119-1138). The counted proof is a genuine reduction: it passes to the morphism between the fibres, which is flat because it is a base change along a field extension, applies the same-chapter decomposition of associated points over a locally Noetherian base to write the associated points of the fibre upstairs as a union indexed by those of the fibre downstairs, and then identifies the fibre of the fibrewise morphism at a point with the spectrum of the residue field tensor product, whose associated primes are its minimal primes by the cited Noetherian Cohen-Macaulay statement (proof lines 1140-1167). It is H2: the reduction is carried out in the counted span, with the cited inputs being standard fibre, decomposition and algebra facts.
